implementation: Bound DescribeQuorum nested codecs, preflight helpers and nonignorable version fields; cap public Admin retries. Qualify genuine current SDK wire/public behavior and owned native handlers.
strict_checks: four package feature cells each24 compiled documentation examples
limits: Selected current API55 versions0–2, raw message models and public broker-bootstrap Admin methods. Genuine SDK builders/parsers, public Java calls, public Rust calls and native broker handlers qualify this finite cohort. No Apache JUnit class is claimed executed.

The applicability declaration retains30 exact source-method rows and39 exact internal Raft parameter invocations. Internal election/follower timer/snapshot-injection histories remain unqualified by this client card and stay under exhaustive applicability and KRaft server work. Existing historical internal-role exclusions, original pins and182-case denominator are unchanged.

Local codec limits:1MiB complete body,32767 bytes per string/1MiB total,8192 elements per array/32768 total,4MiB requested vector slots plus string copies,64 tags per structure/1024 total and64KiB total tag payload. Required strings/arrays reject nulls; strict UTF8, ordered unique tags and complete consumption are local decoder policies. These are logical admission limits, not allocator capacity or RSS bounds.

Generic BrokerConn transport retains its100MiB frame ceiling and write/read buffering behavior; this card does not establish a1MiB preallocation limit for socket framing, global network memory, OS buffers, secure transport or a resource soak. The nested decoder and encoder/error-helper allocations are bounded before their reservations/copies.

The SDK accepts8193 empty topics; Rust rejects them under its local limit. All SDKs refuse strings above32767 bytes and nonignorable directory IDs/nodes before v2; Rust aligns with those serializer rules. Older error messages and timestamps are omitted according to their gates. Rust skips opaque tags; Java reverse comparisons clear only those tags.

Rust public retries share one total operation deadline and stop after8 attempts, returning the last broker/transport error. Java retry-exhaustion runs to its operation deadline. The300ms deadline/exhaustion profiles explicitly record one genuine success warm-up on each Admin instance before the measured operation. Twelve warm-ups per feature build are retained, parsed and excluded from timed attempt counts.

Six fresh singleton combined Kafka broker/controllers across the two feature builds execute raw API55v0/v1/v2 and public highest-shared-version2 calls through an owned recording proxy. Each native public result matches its own captured SDK-decoded response, including the changing high watermark. No native controller failover, multi-voter state or partitionline Kafka server is inferred.

All scripted and proxy threads/sockets join and listener ports are rebound. Every native broker is parent-waited after TERM and exits143; native broker/controller ports are closed and rebound. Native bin/libs/config hashes independently match each retained release archive. JVM identity is observed and unchanged during retention; Rust ELF, source and jar inputs have complete before/after guards. Full host shared-library attestation is outside scope.

Actual old-source regression failed5 of6 ordinary checks; its exact source and executed ELF are retained. Shared-cache misuse, compiler/lint failures, initial common-peer version-field failures with their executed ELF, prototype SDK Disconnect result, and the cold Java deadline without API55 dispatch remain recorded. Later complete qualified attempts do not erase those failures.

Latest stable Rust1.99.0 only. Full source-bound suites, strict default/all Clippy, formatting/rustdoc and four extracted package consumers pass. This does not establish production readiness or any performance ranking; core/full conformance and Suite HOLD remain incomplete.
